body.p: Applicant has reviewed the final Office action dated July 15, 2021, and the references cited therein. Claims 1-16 are currently pending. Claims 1-13 currently stand rejected. Claims 14-16 are withdrawn from consideration.
Applicant's Amendments

Applicant, in response to the continued rejection of the claims based upon an unintended broad interpretation of Applicant's previously claimed "carrier" structure recited in independent claim 1, has clarified claim 1 to expressly recite that the carrier is configured such that, in use, the carrier fits fully around a human body at the thoracic region of the human body. The current claim language clarifications preclude reading the claim to cover a carrier that does not extend fully around the human body (i.e. Derkx's carrier that, in use, traverses only partway around a human body).

Applicant has further amended independent claim 1 to expressly recite that the electrodes are configured to simultaneously acquire electric physiological signals from the human body. See Applicant's original specification, at page 12, line 22 to page 13, line 12. This clarification expressly distinguishes over the teachings of the cited reference that would require moving the electrode to a second position, after taking a first reading at a first location, and subsequently taking a second reading at a different point in time (i.e., non-simultaneous multiple readings).
Applicant's current amendments preclude a broad interpretation of Applicant's claim 1 upon which the final Office action sustains the previous rejection of independent claim 1.
Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the grounds for rejection of the

previously pending claims in view of Applicant's further amendments to the claims and remarks addressing the shortcomings of the prior art with regard to particular recited elements of the claimed invention.
Please charge any fee deficiencies to Deposit Account No. 12-1216. Grounds for Rejecting the Claims
1. Claims 1-4, 11 and 13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Derkx, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0360329 (Derkx) in view of Tupin, U.S. Pub. No. 2011/0060215 (Tupin).
2. Claims 5-6 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Derkx in view of Tupin as applied to claim 1, and further in view of McGrane, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0019988 (McGrane).
3. Claim 7 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Derkx in view of Tupin as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Maesani, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0273590 (Maesani).
4. Claims 8 and 10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over the
combined teachings of Derkx, Tupin and Maesani as applied to claim 7, and in further view of Muccio, U.S. Pub. No. 2012/0016440 (Muccio).
5. Claim 9 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Derkx in view of Tupin as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Hsiao, U.S. Pub. No. 2012/0265025 (Hsiao).
6. Claim 12 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Derkx in view of Tupin as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Sims, U.S. Pub. No. 2007/0293781 (Sims).
Applicant traverses the grounds for each and every rejection for at least the reasons set forth herein below. Applicant addresses the specific rejections in the order they arise in the Office Action.
Applicant's Specific Responses to the Grounds for Rejection
1. Rejection of Claims 1-4, 11 and 13 as being obvious over Derkx in view of Tupin

Applicant, at least in view of the current further clarifying amendments to independent claim 1, traverses the rejection of claims 1-4, 11 and 13, as being obvious over the teachings of Derkx in view of Tupin. A prima facie case of obviousness cannot be established with regard to any one of the currently pending claims since the combined teachings of the cited Derkx and Tupin references do not describe each recited element of any currently pending independent claim. Notably, neither reference describes applicant's further clarified "carrier" structure that, in use, fits fully around a human body at a thoracic region part. Nor do either of the two references describe electrodes that are configured to simultaneously acquire electric physiologic signal from the human body.
Moreover, a proper reason cannot be established for one skilled in the art to modify

Derkx's teachings, in view of Tupin, in a way that would result in Applicant's claimed invention. Notably, neither reference demonstrates any awareness of a particularized problem that would provide a reason to modify Derkx (in view of Tupin) in a way that resulted in Applicant's claimed invention.
a. Applicant's Claimed Invention

Applicant's claimed invention is directed to an arrangement that uses a carrier, fully surrounding a human body, to hold a plurality of electrodes on a patient's body. In particular claim 1, provided in clean form below, recites:
A wearable device for monitoring one or more vital signs of a human
body, the wearable device comprising:
a carrier configured to fit, while in use, fully around the human body, at
an abdominal part thereof; and
an electrode arrangement comprising a plurality of conductive electrodes,
wherein the electrodes are arranged on the carrier to be brought in contact with a

skin of the body in use, and wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes are configured for operating simultaneously to receive electric physiologic signals from the body for enabling monitoring of a membrane potential of one or more
muscles in the body,
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes arranged on the carrier
comprise one or more first electrodes arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a side part of a torso of the body, to receive via said first electrodes a first
electrical signal indicative of a membrane potential of a thoracic diaphragm of the
body;
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes arranged on the carrier
further comprises at least one second electrode in addition to the one or more
first electrodes, the at least one second electrode being arranged on the carrier to
be in contact with a mid front part of the abdominal part of the body, and to be aligned with the one or more first electrodes, the at least one second electrode
thereby being arranged for receiving a second electrical signal indicative of one or
more further electric physiologic signals from the body, for enabling filtering of
the first electrical signal using the second electrical signal for enabling
electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm. (Emphasis added).

Thus, Applicant's claimed invention provides a sensor arrangement that is uniquely arranged for monitoring respiration activity of pre-term born babies. See Applicant's Specification, page 1, lines 14-22. In stark contrast to using adhesive-mounted patches, in

accordance with Applicant's claimed invention, a carrier is placed fully around a patient's abdomen that holds multiple electrodes in place. See Applicant's Specification, at page 2, lines 4-11. Per Applicant's further clarification, the carrier fully surrounds the body at a thoracic part of the body (the abdominal region). See page 4, lines 11-19.
Moreover, a sensor electrode arrangement, per Applicant's current clarifications, is

recited that addresses a technical problem (signal degradation) that arises from using a carrier that fully surrounds the human body, in place of adhesive patches (per Derkx). Specifically, the presence of a higher contact impedance - and hence weaker signals. In particular, the electric physiological signal from the thoracic diaphragm is very weak and distorted by many other signals from the body. See page 2, lines 13-20. Per Applicant's claimed invention, in order to enable an EMG to be provided, an improved signal-to-noise ratio is needed to provide a reliable measurement. See Applicant's Specification, at page 2, lines 18-20. Applicant's claimed invention overcomes the aforementioned technical problem by the at least one second electrode that provides a signal for filtering the first electrical signal.

The claimed filtering of the first electrical signal using the simultaneously acquired signal of the second electrode is described extensively by Applicant's specification at page 3, line 21 to page 4, line 19. Applicant's claimed filtering of the first electrode signal using the second electrode results in a signal having a higher SNR. The resulting higher SNR, in turn, enables use the claimed carrier (fully surrounding the abdomen of the body) instead of a patch (per Derkx). The second electrode furthermore enables obtaining an ECG of the patient. All the above distinctions (and resulting advantages) are neither described nor contemplated by the teachings of the cited references discussed herein below.
b. The teachings of the cited References

As noted in Applicant's previous response, neither Derkx nor Tupin particularly focusses on the challenges of monitoring preterm babies, and neither teaches or suggests Applicant's claimed carrier that fits fully around the human body or the particular solution to a technical problem arising from such physical carrier configuration.

Derkx, upon which the Office action primarily relies, describes an adhesive patch placed upon a patient that holds a sensor in place upon a patient's body. FIG. 1 is reproduced below for convenient reference.
Moreover, Derkx does not describe Applicant's claimed multi-electrode arrangement on a single carrier, in particular:
an electrode arrangement comprising a plurality of conductive electrodes,
wherein the electrodes are arranged on the carrier to be brought in contact with a

skin of the body in use, and wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes are configured for operating simultaneously to receive electric physiologic signals from the body for enabling monitoring of a membrane potential of one or more
muscles in the body...." Emphasis added.
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes arranged on the carrier
comprise one or more first electrodes arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a side part of a torso of the body, to receive via said first electrodes a first
electrical signal indicative of a membrane potential of a thoracic diaphragm of the
body;
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes arranged on the carrier
further comprises at least one second electrode in addition to the one or more
first electrodes, the at least one second electrode being arranged on the carrier to
be in contact with a mid front part of the abdominal part of the body, and to be aligned with the one or more first electrodes, the at least one second electrode
thereby being arranged for receiving a second electrical signal indicative of one or
more further electric physiologic signals from the body, for enabling filtering of
the first electrical signal using the second electrical signal for enabling
electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm. (Emphasis added).
Reference is made to figure 4 of Derkx, and to paragraph [0066] which can be read in connection with paragraph [0021] cited in the Action. Figure 4 of Derkx has been included below.
Preferred placement position for an electromyography patch is indicated by
reference number 64, wherein 64a and 64b represent the two positions for contacting areas 44 of patch 42 to be placed at a second intercostal space,
preferably symmetrically with respect to the sternum of patient 50. [.....] A single
patch 42 may be used wherein the dimensions of the patch 42 correspond
essentially to the borders of placement position 64 and the two points 64a and
64b indicate the position of contacting electrodes 44."

The claimed invention, however, applies first electrodes in contact with "a side part of a torso" and a second electrode in contact "with a mid front part" of the abdomen, and requires this second electrode to be "aligned with the one or more first electrodes". The latter enabling them to be suitably arranged on the carrier which extends fully around the body. Additionally, as confirmed in the previous Office action, Derkx is not directed to "enabling electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm". As such, Derkx does not teach the filtering of the first electric signal by using the second electric signal.
Moreover, the above-discussed distinguishing features of Applicant's clarified

claims are not present in the teachings of Tupin, upon which the final Office action relies to fill admitted gaps in Derkx's teachings with regard to Applicant's previously claimed invention. The final Office action refers to paragraph [0011] of Tupin, which makes clear
that Tupin relies on "implanted electrodes" that, alone, should disqualify Tupin's teachings as being relevant to proposed modifications to Derkx to render Applicant's claimed invention.
Tupin (see e.g., Fig. 4 and paragraphs [0145] through [0148]) describes an ultrawideband medical radar module (UWBMR) that transmits an electromagnetic signal S into the body to a

target area T, using transmission antenna 30. A reflected signal S' is picked up with a receiver antenna 40 that can be analyzed. The electrodes thus do not measure electric physiological signals - in particular not a membrane potential of one or more muscles. Tupin thus does not enable performing electromyography (EMG), and for that reason alone should not be considered for combination with the teachings of Derkx to render Applicant's claimed invention.
c. The Combined teachings of the cited references do not render the claimed invention
Applicant, for at least the reasons provided above (including clarifying amendments
specifically addressing the points raised in the final Office action), traverses the rejection of independent claim 1. As noted specifically above, neither reference describes several elements of

the claimed invention. Importantly, Derkx uses patches that obviate any need to incorporate several elements of Applicant's claimed invention that are particularly useful for a "carrier" based arrangement - as opposed to a "patch" based arrangement for holding sensors to a patient's body to take appropriate readings. As such, there is no indication of a particularized
problem in either cited reference that would lead one skilled in the art to modify Derkx in a way that resulted in Applicant's claimed invention.
d. The dependent claims are not rendered obvious by the cited references' teachings
Claims 2-4, 11 and 13 variously depend from independent claim 1, and incorporate each of the elements discussed herein above that are neither described nor suggested in Derkx or
Tupin. Applicant traverses the rejection of dependent claims 2-4, 11 and 13 for at least the reasons discussed above with reference to claim 1.

Applicant reserves the right to provide additional reasons for distinguishing claims 2-4, 11 and 13 from the teachings of the prior art in the event that any further Office action recites new grounds for rejecting claim 2-4, 11 and 13, or any claim from which claims 2-4, 11 and 13 depend.
